rows.selection_reason: The existing evidence is nonexistent, so the first experiment should test a comprehensive multimodal setup to establish baseline performance and isolate key design choices. This configuration tests multiprofile multimodal modeling with pca_n2000 RNA encoder, resnet50 image encoder, transformer aggregation, and concat fusion - critical components that could significantly impact performance. It balances exploration of core modalities and provides evidence on whether multimodal approaches outperform single-modality baselines.

Existing evidence shows config_002 (resnet50 image encoder) achieves 0.579 validation accuracy. The uncertainty lies in whether using a more advanced image encoder (ViT) improves performance. Testing config_017 isolates the effect of the image encoder while keeping aggregation and fusion consistent, allowing direct comparison of ViT vs ResNet. This addresses a critical design choice with minimal parameter changes, maximizing learning efficiency.

Existing evidence shows that using ImageNet ViT-L as the image encoder (config_017) outperforms ResNet50 (config_002). This experiment tests whether changing aggregation from transformer to avgpool (while keeping ViT-L and concat fusion) impacts performance. It isolates the effect of aggregation, a key design choice, and builds on the strong evidence for ViT-L, balancing exploitation of promising directions with exploration of critical components.

The existing evidence shows that using avgpool aggregation (config_003) outperforms transformer aggregation, and imagenet_vit_l image encoder (config_017) improves performance over resnet50. This experiment tests whether switching from concat fusion (used in config_003) to weighted fusion could further improve performance, isolating the effect of fusion strategy while keeping RNA/image encoders and aggregation method constant. This clarifies whether weighted fusion provides additional benefits over simple concatenation in this multimodal setup.

Existing evidence shows that multimodal, multiprofile models with pca_n2000 RNA encoder, imagenet_vit_l image encoder, avgpool aggregation, and weighted fusion achieve high accuracy (0.6352). This experiment tests whether switching the RNA encoder to scvi_n200 (a different representation method) maintains or improves performance, isolating the impact of RNA encoder choice on the high-performing baseline. This addresses key uncertainty about representation design while building on a promising direction.

The existing evidence shows that using scvi_n200 RNA encoder and imagenet_vit_l image encoder with avgpool aggregation and weighted fusion (config_046) achieves the highest accuracy so far. This experiment tests whether switching aggregation from avgpool to transformer (while keeping other components from config_046) improves performance, isolating the impact of aggregation method. This is a logical extension of the current top-performing configuration and addresses a key design choice with potential to either confirm or refine the optimal approach.

Existing evidence shows that using scvi_n200 RNA encoder, imagenet_vit_l image encoder, transformer aggregation, and weighted fusion achieves high accuracy (0.725). This experiment tests whether replacing the image encoder with resnet50 (while keeping other parameters the same) impacts performance, isolating the effect of the image encoder choice. This clarifies whether the previously observed success depends on the specific image encoder, balancing exploration of critical design choices with exploitation of promising directions.

Existing evidence shows that multimodal, multiprofile setups with scvi_n200 RNA and imagenet_vit_l image encoders (e.g., config_006) achieve high accuracy. This experiment tests replacing imagenet_vit_l with resnet50 while keeping RNA encoder as pca_n2000, aggregation as transformer, and fusion as weighted. It isolates the impact of image encoder choice, a key design decision, to determine if resnet50 could match or exceed imagenet_vit_l's performance in this context.

Existing evidence shows that using scvi_n200 RNA encoder with imagenet_vit_l image encoder, transformer aggregation, and weighted fusion (config_006) achieves the highest accuracy so far. This experiment tests whether switching to scgpt RNA encoder (while keeping other parameters the same) improves performance, isolating the effect of the RNA encoder. This is the best use of the next experiment as it directly evaluates a critical design choice with minimal changes, balancing exploration and exploitation.

Existing evidence shows that using scvi_n200 RNA encoder with imagenet_vit_l image encoder and weighted fusion achieves high accuracy (0.724989). This experiment tests the impact of switching to resnet50 image encoder and avgpool aggregation while keeping scvi_n200 RNA and weighted fusion. It isolates the effect of image encoder and aggregation method, which are critical factors, and could reveal if simpler components (resnet50/avgpool) outperform complex ones (imagenet_vit_l/transformer) in this context.
